question: Minimize the total completion time of six jobs processed on three machines, where each job must be assigned to exactly one of six schedule positions and each position must have exactly one job. The processing times for each job on each machine are as follows: Job 0 takes 5, 5, and 7 hours on Machines 0, 1, and 2 respectively; Job 1 takes 5, 9, and 10 hours; Job 2 takes 6, 7, and 10 hours; Job 3 takes 8, 7, and 9 hours; Job 4 takes 9, 5, and 9 hours; and Job 5 takes 8, 8, and 7 hours. Each job must start on Machine 1 only after completing on Machine 0, and on Machine 2 only after completing on Machine 1. Additionally, the start time of a job in a later position must be at least the start time of the job in the previous position plus its processing time on the same machine. The objective is to minimize the total completion time, which includes the start time of the last job on the last machine plus its processing time. All start times must be non-negative, and job assignments to positions are binary (either assigned or not). The specific coefficients for the objective function are 5, 6, 10, 7, 8, and 8 for JobSchedule[0,5], JobSchedule[1,5], JobSchedule[2,5], JobSchedule[3,5], JobSchedule[4,5], and JobSchedule[5,5] respectively, with an additional term StartTime[5,3]. The constraints include ensuring one job per schedule position, one schedule position per job, machine precedence, and job precedence, with exact coefficients as detailed in the LP data.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# All numeric constants from the problem statement.
DATA = {
    "num_jobs": 6,
    "num_machines": 3,
    "num_positions": 6,
    # processing[job][machine] with rows = jobs, columns = machines
    "processing": [
        [5, 5, 7],   # Job 0 takes 5, 5, and 7 hours on Machines 0, 1, and 2 respectively
        [5, 9, 10],  # Job 1 takes 5, 9, and 10 hours
        [6, 7, 10],  # Job 2 takes 6, 7, and 10 hours
        [8, 7, 9],   # Job 3 takes 8, 7, and 9 hours
        [9, 5, 9],   # Job 4 takes 9, 5, and 9 hours
        [8, 8, 7],   # Job 5 takes 8, 8, and 7 hours
    ],
    # objective coefficients on x[j, last_position]
    "obj_coeff": [5, 6, 10, 7, 8, 8],
    # big-M for linearising the position-precedence product
    "big_m": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n_jobs = d["num_jobs"]
    n_mach = d["num_machines"]
    n_pos = d["num_positions"]
    proc = d["processing"]
    coeff = d["obj_coeff"]
    big_m = d["big_m"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_jobs - 1)      # jobs
    model.M = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_mach - 1)      # machines
    model.K = pyo.RangeSet(0, n_pos - 1)       # schedule positions

    # Binary assignment: x[j,k] = 1 if job j assigned to position k
    # "each job must be assigned to exactly one of six schedule positions"
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.J, model.K, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Start times s[k,m]: start time of the job in position k on machine m
    # "All start times must be non-negative"
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.K, model.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # One job per schedule position
    # "each position must have exactly one job"
    def one_job_per_position_rule(m, k):
        return sum(m.x[j, k] for j in m.J) == 1
    model.one_job_per_position = pyo.Constraint(model.K, rule=one_job_per_position_rule)

    # One schedule position per job
    # "each job must be assigned to exactly one of six schedule positions"
    def one_position_per_job_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[j, k] for k in m.K) == 1
    model.one_position_per_job = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=one_position_per_job_rule)

    # Machine precedence: s[k,m+1] >= s[k,m] + processing on machine m
    # "Each job must start on Machine 1 only after completing on Machine 0,
    #  and on Machine 2 only after completing on Machine 1."
    # The processing time depends on which job is in position k, so we
    # linearise: s[k,m+1] >= s[k,m] + sum_j proc[j][m] * x[j,k]
    def machine_precedence_rule(m, k, mach):
        if mach == n_mach - 1:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.s[k, mach + 1] >= m.s[k, mach] + sum(
            proc[j][mach] * m.x[j, k] for j in m.J
        )
    model.machine_precedence = pyo.Constraint(model.K, model.M, rule=machine_precedence_rule)

    # Position precedence: s[k,m] >= s[k-1,m] + processing of job in position k-1 on machine m
    # "the start time of a job in a later position must be at least the start time
    #  of the job in the previous position plus its processing time on the same machine"
    # The processing time of the job in position k-1 is sum_j proc[j][m]*x[j,k-1].
    def position_precedence_rule(m, k, mach):
        if k == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.s[k, mach] >= m.s[k - 1, mach] + sum(
            proc[j][mach] * m.x[j, k - 1] for j in m.J
        )
    model.position_precedence = pyo.Constraint(model.K, model.M, rule=position_precedence_rule)

    # Objective: minimize makespan = completion time of last job on last machine
    # "minimize the total completion time, which includes the start time of the
    #  last job on the last machine plus its processing time."
    # Coefficients 5,6,10,7,8,8 on x[j,last_position] plus s[last_position,last_machine]
    last_pos = n_pos - 1
    last_mach = n_mach - 1
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(coeff[j] * model.x[j, last_pos] for j in model.J)
        + model.s[last_pos, last_mach],
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    return model

    # objective coefficients for last position (processing on last machine)

    jobs = range(d["num_jobs"])
    machines = range(d["num_machines"])
    positions = range(d["num_positions"])
    p = d["processing"]
    last_machine = d["num_machines"] - 1
    last_position = d["num_positions"] - 1
    M = d["big_m"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.Jobs = pyo.Set(initialize=jobs)
    model.Machines = pyo.Set(initialize=machines)
    model.Positions = pyo.Set(initialize=positions)

    # x[j,k] = 1 if job j assigned to position k
    # "each job must be assigned to exactly one of six schedule positions"
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.Jobs, model.Positions, within=pyo.Binary)

    # s[k,m] = start time of job in position k on machine m
    # "All start times must be non-negative"
    # assumption: start_time_variable_domain = NonNegativeReals
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.Positions, model.Machines, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: minimize makespan = completion of last job on last machine
    # "The objective is to minimize the total completion time, which includes the
    #  start time of the last job on the last machine plus its processing time."
    # assumption: objective_interpretation_total_completion_time = minimize makespan
    def obj_rule(m):
        expr = m.s[last_position, last_machine]
        for j in m.Jobs:
            expr += d["obj_coeffs_last_position"][j] * m.x[j, last_position]
        return expr
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each position has exactly one job
    # "each position must have exactly one job"
    def one_job_per_position_rule(m, k):
        return sum(m.x[j, k] for j in m.Jobs) == 1
    model.one_job_per_position = pyo.Constraint(

    )

    # Each job assigned to exactly one position

    def one_position_per_job_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[j, k] for k in m.Positions) == 1
    model.one_position_per_job = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Jobs, rule=one_position_per_job_rule
    )

    # Machine precedence: s[k,m+1] >= s[k,m] + processing on machine m

            return pyo.Constraint.Skip

        return m.s[k, mm + 1] >= m.s[k, mm] + proc
    model.machine_precedence = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Positions, model.Machines, rule=machine_precedence_rule
